To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Spanish economic system, and especially the labor market, is not flexible enough.
the Spanish economy has been hit by the current financial crisis because the labor market is not flexible, but because it has been too flexible.
labor flexibility, inequality, and financial crisis are all interrelated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship among labor market flexibility, income distribution, and financial crises.
the relationship between labor flexibility, inequality, and financial crisis in Spain.
the following question: What are the causes of the high unemployment in Spain?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current economic crisis is the result of the interaction between the global financial crisis and a labor market model that has not been able to cope with its own internal contradictions.
the Spanish labor market reforms have been a major cause of the current economic problems.
the current economic crisis in Spain is a result of a combination of the global crisis and the domestic labor market crisis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the labor flexibility measures adopted in Spain since 1984 have not been able to reduce the unemployment rate, but rather have contributed to increasing inequality, and have also been a key factor in the deep impact of global financial crisis on the Spanish economy.

the current economic situation is a consequence of the lack of a long term strategy in Spain to promote a sustainable economic growth, which would allow to increase productivity and employment, while reducing income inequality.
the Spanish economy has been in a state of permanent crisis since the 1980s.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the labor reforms introduced during the past three decades, which have been praised as a success story in terms of job creation, are not a good recipe to overcome the current unemployment crisis in Spain.
the current crisis is not only a financial one but also a crisis of the Spanish model of capitalism.
labor flexibility, when not properly regulated, may be the source of a financial crisis.
